decisions.reason: The two-component injection unit draws on the firm's core in-house engineering and was visibly committed with its own page, so management would attribute any weak results to temporary pandemic effects and persist.
As a second injection unit in a line the firm has invested in and promoted, it fits the announced direction of customized application technology and justifies continued commitment.
Automatic airless guns are central to the firm's spray application identity and complement its pump systems, so dropping one would contradict earlier investment and its public positioning.
A manual airless gun is a staple accessory that sells alongside the core equipment, and it has a dedicated page and low ongoing cost, so management keeps it.
The air-assisted airless gun extends the core spray portfolio the firm has publicly committed to, and any disappointing uptake can be blamed on temporary market conditions.

Visibility fell from a dedicated page to a mere mention, which signals weaker commitment, but the data logger supports the firm's innovation narrative, so management persists despite a moderate risk of withdrawal.
